# Dashboard

## Use when
- The user opens the product to learn how things are going: usage, revenue, deployments, activity over a period.
- Several metrics, one chart and a detail list belong on one screen with shared filters.

## Don't use when
- One record's fields are shown. That is a `Card`, not a dashboard.
- The screen is a long sortable list of records. That is the Data table pattern.
- The user must act on each item (approve, triage). Use a list with actions, not metric cards.

## Decision rules
- Order top to bottom: filters (date range first) → KPI row → chart and detail table. On desktop the chart and the table share one row; on a phone they stack, chart first. Every number on the screen answers to the filters at the top. Why: Zoho, Mintlify and StackAI lead with a date range and KPI row.
- Filters: a `Select` of range presets (Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Custom range), a `DatePicker` for the custom range, a `Switch` labelled "Compare to previous period", and an outline `Button` for Export.
- Each KPI is a `StatCard`: the label, the period, the value and a delta with its comparison period ("Up 12% vs previous period") with the word up or down, not colour alone. `StatCard` supplies the Card, the delta Badge and the loading skeletons; do not rebuild them.
- Always state the period of a metric ("6h", "Last 7 days"). Why: Vercel overview cards label each period.
- Chart: one `Chart` per question at its natural width (the plot is fixed), a title that says what it shows, `ChartBar` with an `aria-label` describing the data. Use `Table` for exact values. Never more than one series per chart unless a legend is shown.
- Detail table: `Table` with `TableCaption`, numbers aligned `end`. Link to the Data table pattern when rows exceed one screen.
- Loading → `Skeleton` in the shape of the final content, or `Chart state="loading"`. Empty → say why and offer the next step inside the card ("No recent events", an "Enable analytics" `Button`). A first-use dashboard with no data at all is one empty state (icon, heading, text, one primary `Button`), with no filters or KPI cards above it. Why: Vercel in-card empty states with an action.
- Filters change results without a page reload and show a "Reset" `Button variant="ghost"` once any is set.
- A failed card load → an `Alert variant="danger"` with `actions` (Retry) in place of that card. One failed card never blanks the screen.
- Limit the first view to 4 KPIs and 2 charts. More goes behind `Tabs` (`variant="line"`), not further down the page.

## Components and variants
- `Select` size: `md`
- `DatePicker`
- `Switch` size: `md`
- `Button` variant: `primary`, `ghost`, `outline` · size: `md`
- `StatCard` size: `md`
- `Chart`
- `Table`
- `Skeleton`
- `Alert` variant: `danger` · size: `md`
- `Tabs` variant: `line` · size: `md`

## Layout and density
- A responsive grid: `StatCard`s in an auto-fit row (minimum width from `--atlas-content-width-sm`), spacing `--atlas-spacing-4` between cards and `--atlas-spacing-6` between sections.
- Below the KPIs, the chart (670 px) and the table fill one row, `--atlas-spacing-6` apart. Do not nest Cards.

## Hierarchy and composition
- One page title, then the filter row. The value is the largest text in a KPI; labels and periods are muted.
- The most important metric comes first. Group by question, not by data source.
- Typography: Page title `--atlas-text-h1`; section titles `--atlas-text-h4`; labels, periods and empty-state help `--atlas-text-body-sm` in `foreground-muted`. Set every heading and paragraph from `--atlas-text-*` or `--atlas-font-size-*`; never a bare `<h1>` or `<p>`.

## Responsive behavior
- Phone: filters wrap and stack, KPI cards stack one per row, the chart drops its stats, and the table scrolls horizontally.

## States
- default · loading (Skeleton or `Chart state="loading"`) · empty (explain and offer a step; first-use is the whole dashboard) · error (one Alert per failed card) · filtered (Reset visible).
- stale: show "Updated 2 min ago" when data is cached.

## Accessibility
- Every chart has an `aria-label` and a table or text equivalent. Deltas include the word up or down for screen readers.
- Filter controls are named; changing a filter announces the updated result politely.
- Do not rely on colour for good or bad.

## Anti-patterns
- KPI numbers with no period or comparison.
- Eight or more charts on first load.
- Colour-only deltas, or a chart with no text alternative.
- A spinner over the whole page while one card loads.
- Hardcoded chart colours.

## Example
```tsx
import * as React from "react"
import { Alert } from "@atlas/ui-web/compositions/Alert/Alert"
import { DatePicker, DatePickerContent, DatePickerTrigger, type DatePickerRange } from "@atlas/ui-web/compositions/DatePicker/DatePicker"
import { StatCard } from "@atlas/ui-web/compositions/StatCard/StatCard"
import { Chart, ChartContent, ChartDescription, ChartHeader, ChartTitle, ChartBar } from "@atlas/ui-web/compositions/Chart/Chart"
import { Button } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Button/Button"
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Select/Select"
import { Switch } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Switch/Switch"
import { Skeleton } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Skeleton/Skeleton"
import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Table/Table"

type Kpi = { label: string; value: string; delta: number }
type Row = { page: string; views: number }

const PERIODS: Record<string, string> = { "24h": "Last 24 hours", "7d": "Last 7 days", "30d": "Last 30 days", custom: "Custom range" }

export function UsageDashboard({ kpis, series, pages, loading, error, range, onRange, custom, onCustom, compare, onCompare, onConnect, onRetry }: {
  kpis: Kpi[]
  series: Array<{ date: string; visitors: number }>
  pages: Row[]
  loading: boolean
  error: boolean
  range: string
  onRange: (v: string) => void
  custom: DatePickerRange
  onCustom: (r: DatePickerRange) => void
  compare: boolean
  onCompare: (v: boolean) => void
  onConnect: () => void
  onRetry: () => void
}) {
  // First use: nothing is connected, so there is nothing to filter. One empty state, one next step.
  if (!loading && kpis.length === 0) {
    return (
      <div role="status" style={{ display: "grid", justifyItems: "center", textAlign: "center", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-3)", paddingBlock: "var(--atlas-spacing-12)" }}>
        <h2 style={{ fontSize: "var(--atlas-text-h3)" }}>No data yet</h2>
        <p style={{ fontSize: "var(--atlas-text-body-sm)", color: "var(--atlas-foreground-muted)" }}>Connect a data source to see visitors, revenue and activity here.</p>
        <Button variant="primary" onClick={onConnect}>Connect a data source</Button>
      </div>
    )
  }
  const periodLabel = PERIODS[range]
  return (
    <div style={{ display: "grid", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-6)" }}>
      <div style={{ display: "flex", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-3)", alignItems: "center" }}>
        <div style={{ flex: "0 1 12rem" }}>
          <Select value={range} onValueChange={onRange}>
            <SelectTrigger aria-label="Date range"><SelectValue placeholder="Date range" /></SelectTrigger>
            <SelectContent>
              <SelectItem value="24h">Last 24 hours</SelectItem>
              <SelectItem value="7d">Last 7 days</SelectItem>
              <SelectItem value="30d">Last 30 days</SelectItem>
              <SelectItem value="custom">Custom range</SelectItem>
            </SelectContent>
          </Select>
        </div>
        <div style={{ flex: "0 1 15rem" }}>
          <DatePicker mode="range" value={custom} onValueChange={(v) => { onCustom(v); onRange("custom") }}>
            <DatePickerTrigger aria-label="Custom date range" placeholder="Pick a range" />
            <DatePickerContent />
          </DatePicker>
        </div>
        <Switch label="Compare to previous period" checked={compare} onCheckedChange={onCompare} />
        <span style={{ flex: 1 }} />
        {(range !== "7d" || compare) && <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => { onRange("7d"); onCompare(false) }}>Reset</Button>}
        <Button variant="outline">Export</Button>
      </div>

      <div style={{ display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(auto-fit, minmax(var(--atlas-content-width-sm), 1fr))", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-4)" }}>
        {kpis.map((k) => (
          <StatCard
            key={k.label}
            label={k.label}
            period={periodLabel}
            value={k.value}
            loading={loading}
            delta={{ text: k.delta === 0 ? "vs previous period" : `${Math.abs(k.delta)}% vs previous period`, trend: k.delta > 0 ? "up" : k.delta < 0 ? "down" : "flat" }}
          />
        ))}
      </div>

      {/* Chart and table share a row on desktop and stack on a phone. The chart keeps its natural width. */}
      <div style={{ display: "flex", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-6)", alignItems: "flex-start" }}>
        <div style={{ flex: "0 1 670px", minWidth: 0, inlineSize: "100%", maxInlineSize: "670px" }}>
        {error ? (
          <Alert variant="danger" title="We couldn't load visitors" description="The other cards are unaffected."
            actions={<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={onRetry}>Retry</Button>} />
        ) : (
          <Chart state={loading ? "loading" : series.length === 0 ? "empty" : "default"}>
            <ChartHeader>
              <ChartTitle>Visitors</ChartTitle>
              <ChartDescription>Daily visitors for the selected range</ChartDescription>
            </ChartHeader>
            <ChartContent emptyMessage="No visitors in this range">
              <ChartBar aria-label="Visitors per day" data={series} xKey="date" dataKey="visitors" label="Visitors" />
            </ChartContent>
          </Chart>
        )}
        </div>
        <section aria-labelledby="top-pages" style={{ flex: "1 1 20rem", minWidth: 0, display: "grid", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-3)" }}>
          <h2 id="top-pages" style={{ fontSize: "var(--atlas-text-h4)" }}>Top pages</h2>
          <div style={{ overflowX: "auto" }}>
            {loading ? <Skeleton /> : (
              <Table>
                <TableCaption>Page views in the selected range</TableCaption>
                <TableHeader>
                  <TableRow><TableHead>Page</TableHead><TableHead align="end">Views</TableHead></TableRow>
                </TableHeader>
                <TableBody>
                  {pages.map((p) => (
                    <TableRow key={p.page}><TableCell>{p.page}</TableCell><TableCell align="end">{p.views}</TableCell></TableRow>
                  ))}
                </TableBody>
              </Table>
            )}
          </div>
        </section>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```
